question: Events $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive and satisfy $P(A)>0$ and $P(B)>0$. Examine whether $A$ and $B$ can be independent. Give mathematical justification.
explanation:
Step 1: Consequence of mutual exclusiveness
Since $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, they cannot occur simultaneously. Therefore, $$A\cap B=\varnothing$$ and hence $$P(A\cap B)=0.$$
Step 2: Independence condition
If $A$ and $B$ were independent, they would have to satisfy $$P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B).$$
Step 3: Use of the positive probabilities
It is given that $P(A)>0$ and $P(B)>0$. Therefore, their product must also be positive, so $$P(A)P(B)>0.$$
Step 4: Comparison of the two results
Mutual exclusiveness gives $P(A\cap B)=0$, whereas independence would require $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)>0$. These two conditions cannot hold simultaneously.
Step 5: Conclusion
Hence, two mutually exclusive events having non-zero probabilities $$\boxed{\text{cannot be independent}}.$$

options.A: They can be independent because $P(A\cap B)=P(A)+P(B)$
options.B: They can be independent only when $P(A)=P(B)$
options.C: They cannot be independent because mutual exclusiveness gives $P(A\cap B)=0$, while $P(A)P(B)>0$
options.D: They are always independent because mutually exclusive events cannot occur together
